play_name: Show the real you and see who fits
behavioral_target: Changing yourself to match what other people seem to want.
trigger: When you want someone to like you.
old_play: You shift who you are — your opinions, likes, and needs — to fit them.
function_of_old_play: It helps you fit in and keep their interest right now.
new_play: Show a small true part of you instead — a real opinion, like, or need — and watch how they take it.
what_to_expect: It can feel risky, and some people may step back. That is real information.
why_supports_task: Discernment means seeing clearly. When the other person meets the real you, you can tell if you two truly fit.
maintaining_behaviors_consolidated: Changing yourself for other people to fit in and be liked.
context_limitations: Small, steady steps are fine. This is not about oversharing with someone you don't trust yet.

play_name: Choose your dating breaks on purpose
behavioral_target: Not re-engaging with dating apps after feeling discouraged.
trigger: After dating feels tiring or lets you down.
old_play: You don't get the apps again because you don't feel like it.
function_of_old_play: It gives you a break from dating that feels hard right now.
new_play: Notice if the break is a rest you chose or a way to avoid dating because it feels hopeless. Pick how long to rest, then check in with yourself.
what_to_expect: You may have to sit with the tired, let-down feeling instead of just avoiding it.
why_supports_task: Discernment means choosing on purpose. A chosen rest helps you reset; drifting away by default can keep you stuck.
maintaining_behaviors_consolidated: Pulling back from dating apps when discouraged.
context_limitations: Resting on purpose is healthy. This only becomes a problem if the pullback is avoidance you didn't really choose.
review_reason: Single, near-feeling statement with a conditional alternative; meaning depends on whether the break is chosen rest or avoidance.
